picker.albumsDesc: Camera, screenshots and the other albums on the phone
picker.folderDesc: Any folder on the phone, an SD card or a cloud drive
picker.permissionNeeded: To list the albums on this phone the app needs permission to read photos. Photos are only processed on this phone, never uploaded.
picker.noAlbums: There are no photos on this phone yet.
picker.partial: You allowed access to some photos only, so the albums show just those. Select more on the right, or allow all photos in system settings.
picker.permissionBlocked: Access to photos is turned off and Android will not ask again. In system settings, open Permissions → Photos and videos and choose Always allow all; the albums appear when you come back. Photos are processed on this phone only and never uploaded.
picker.permissionLead: Next, Android will ask for permission to read photos, so the albums on this phone can be listed.
picker.promise1: Scoring and grouping happen on this phone only; nothing is uploaded
picker.promise2: Originals are never moved or modified
picker.promise3: You can allow only some photos, and change it any time in system settings

paused.hot: The phone is getting hot, so the analysis is paused; it picks up again once it cools down, and nothing analysed so far is lost.
paused.battery: The battery is below 15%, so the analysis is paused; it picks up again once the phone is charging, and nothing analysed so far is lost.

settings.analysisHow: The app picks the model and the hardware for your phone: phones with 12 GB of memory or more and many cores use the more accurate large model, the others the faster standard one; when the phone's neural processor (NNAPI) gives the same answers as the CPU it is used. To use a more accurate model, download “High-quality analysis” under Downloaded models.
settings.privacyBody: Photos are processed on this phone only and are never uploaded.
settings.projectMade: Project created; open it under Cull.
settings.modelsBody: The models are downloaded to this phone only when needed and run fully offline afterwards: the same models and manifest as the Mac app.
settings.tierAutoDesc: Decided by this phone's memory and cores

tierDesc.high: More accurate; more sensitive to blur, composition and look

settings.tierHint: After switching, the project in view is re-evaluated.
settings.glassDesc: The tab bar and floating controls refract what is behind them. Off, they are plain frosted panels, smoother on older phones.
settings.learnResetBody: The {{labels}} choices and {{refs}} reference photos it learned from are erased for good. To keep a copy, export your taste under Backup first.
settings.mirrorsDesc: Folders picked from a NAS or a cloud drive keep a copy of their photos on the phone. Clear one and it is fetched again the next time the project opens; the analysis is kept.
settings.diagnosticsDesc: Version, system, settings (no passwords or tokens), recent logs and crash records, saved as one text file where you choose. Whether to send it is up to you.
settings.mirrorClearBody: The project “{{project}}” is open and uses this copy. After clearing, its photos are fetched again from the source, and full-size views are unavailable until then. Analysis results are kept.

cull.hint: Tap a photo to select it; the bar below keeps, rejects or opens it. In single view, push up to keep and pull down to reject.
cull.allowBackground: Stops when you switch apps? Tap to let FleetingGleam run in the background
cull.canLeave: You can leave this page or switch apps; the analysis carries on in the background.
cull.busyBody: One project is analysed at a time. Stop “{{name}}” (nothing analysed is lost; it carries on when you go back) and analyse this one?
cull.offline: NAS “{{name}}” is not connected; showing the photos from the last sync

models.skipBody: The analysis runs without it — no closed-eye check or people for now. You can download it later in Settings → Models & storage.
models.useStandard: Use the standard model for now ({{size}})
models.useStandardDesc: Smaller and quicker; you can switch to a better one later under Settings → Analysis.
models.sampleNote: The sample photos need an analysis model too, so this is the smallest one; once it is here, your own photos need no further download.
models.metered: You are on a metered network (mobile data or a hotspot); this uses about {{size}} of data.
models.useStandardHere: Use the standard model already on the phone

organize.toAlbumDesc: Copy {{count}} to the album "{{where}}"; originals untouched
organize.offline: The NAS is not connected; this needs it
organize.exportCancelled: Stopped: {{count}} exported, the rest left as they were.
organize.exportedSame: {{n}} were already there, identical, and were skipped

start.fact1: Analysed on this phone only; nothing is uploaded
start.fact2: Similar shots are grouped, the best one suggested
start.fact3: Originals are never changed; rejects go to the bin

pset.keepShareOff: Every photo that makes the grade is kept
pset.keepShareOn: Good photos beyond the share go to review
pset.onePerGroupDesc: The others go to review or are rejected

ready.note: Everything runs on this phone; the originals are never changed.
ready.resume: {{done}} already analysed; only the rest are analysed this time.

scan.landing: Photos land here as they are analysed

scan.timeoutBody: {{done}} of {{total}} photos are analysed. Android lets a background analysis run for only 6 hours a day; open the app to carry on, nothing analysed so far is lost.
scan.pausedHot: The phone is too hot, paused ({{done}}/{{total}})

scan.pausedBatteryBody: It carries on by itself once the phone is charging

styles.resetBody: The {{labels}} choices and {{refs}} reference photos it learned from are erased for good; the style itself and the projects using it stay.

err.space: Not enough space: {{need}} is needed and only {{avail}} is free. Free up some space and try again.
err.spaceShort: The phone is out of space. Free up some and try again.
err.verify: The downloaded file is incomplete. Try again.
err.net: Could not reach the download address. Check the network or proxy and try again.
err.auth: The user name or password is wrong. Enter it again in Settings.

nas.authOffline: The user name or password for NAS “{{name}}” is wrong; showing the photos from the last sync
nas.authError: This project is on NAS “{{name}}” and its user name or password is wrong. Enter it again in Settings.
nas.deniedError: This project is on NAS “{{name}}”, and this account is not allowed to access it.

body.detect: Finding the faces in photos on the phone needs a very small model first (about {{size}}); MediaPipe then tells closed eyes and the people apart. Downloaded once, then fully offline; photos are never uploaded.
body.bundle: This needs a few models first (about {{size}} in all). The app picks the ones that suit this phone. They are downloaded once and everything runs offline afterwards; your photos are never uploaded.
body.faces: Telling people apart (“these are the same person”) needs a recognition model first (about {{size}}). Downloaded once, then fully offline. Faces are only compared on this phone and never uploaded.

desc.detect: Finds the faces in photos on the phone, for closed eyes and people
desc.scenetext: Writes a sentence for scenes the vocabulary cannot name, entirely on this phone

cull.emptyBody: Open a folder and {{brand}} scores every photo on this phone, groups similar bursts, and suggests the best of each. Your originals are never moved or modified.
cull.readyBody: Analysis decodes each photo, checks sharpness and exposure, scores it with on-device models, then groups similar shots. Everything runs on this phone and your originals stay untouched.
cull.safExpired: The folder “{{name}}” for this project can no longer be read: access was revoked (by the system, or when app data was cleared). The photos already copied are still here; grant access again to keep syncing.
cull.safWrongFolder: That is not the original folder. Please pick “{{name}}” again.
cull.safNotGranted: That is the right folder, but read access to “{{name}}” was not granted. Please try again; for cloud folders, check that the app is online and signed in.

searchset.info: The first time it is turned on, a search model is downloaded and the photos are indexed in the background (a few tens of milliseconds each). It all happens on this phone; photos are never uploaded.

styles.fromFolderInfo: The photos in that folder count as “the kind I choose”, and your taste is learned on this phone from them, so you need not mark photos one by one. Only a description of each photo is kept, never the photo, and nothing is uploaded.

picker.localDesc: Phone storage, an SD card or a cloud drive

settings.analysisAutoDesc: The app picks the model and the hardware that suit this phone; there is nothing to set.
settings.eyeMethodDesc: On the phone, MediaPipe is used: a small model Google trained that looks at the face closely and tells a laughing squint from an actual closed eye. The face position comes from the on-device face detector, and it all runs only on this phone.
settings.backupInfo: What is backed up is exactly what “my settings and taste” exports: the app settings and what each style has learned (vectors and decisions); no photos, projects or paths. About 20 seconds after a setting or a taste changes it is uploaded again; “Back up now” triggers that same upload by hand. The bucket keeps the latest copy plus one per day, only the most recent ones (how many is up to you). You create an R2 bucket in the Cloudflare dashboard yourself, with an API token that can only read and write that bucket; the secret is kept encrypted on this phone.
settings.backupRemoveBody: This only forgets the destination and its credentials on this phone; the backups in the bucket are kept.
settings.nasInfo: Connected with the app's own built-in SMB client; the password is kept encrypted on this phone. A project's photos are first copied into the app's own cache and analysed from there (the first opening waits for that; later only new photos are fetched); viewing and exporting use that copy. A NAS has no Trash: rejected photos are moved, on the share, to a ".FleetingGleam Recycle Bin" folder at its root, by day, where they can be restored by hand. Removing a NAS also deletes the copies on the phone; the photos on the NAS are untouched.
settings.nasRemember: Remember the password (kept encrypted on this phone)
settings.nasRemoveBody: This forgets the NAS and its password on this phone and deletes the local mirror copies; the photos on the NAS are untouched. Projects made from it will not open until it is added again.
settings.exportTasteDesc: Save it as one file to import on another phone or on the Mac; a file from someone else can be imported too.
settings.privacyBody: Photos are processed on this phone only. Nothing is uploaded.
settings.learnShort: Learns your taste from what you keep and reject. Stays on this phone.
settings.learnDesc: Learns your taste on this phone from the photos you keep and reject by hand, and uses it to nudge scores. What it learns stays on this device, is never uploaded, and can be reset any time.
settings.modelsBody: The models used for analysis are downloaded to this phone when first needed and run entirely offline; they are the same models, from the same list, as on the Mac.

organize.trashDesc: {{count}} · can be restored from the system bin for 30 days
organize.trashBody: These photos will be moved to the system bin and disappear from this project. For 30 days they can be restored from the bin in your gallery or Files app.
organize.trashRecover: To get them back, open the bin in your gallery or Files app, select the photos and tap Restore.
organize.trashItem: Move rejected photos to the bin…
